newsitem.title: USA: N2K hires Phil Ramone to head new label.
newsitem.headline: N2K hires Phil Ramone to head new label.

text.p: N2K Inc. Monday named Grammy-award winning producer Phil Ramone to head its newly formed N2K Encoded Music division, an independent record label combining online technology with state-of-the-art music production.

Each of the label's titles will be produced in the "enhanced CD," or ECD, format which can be played on all standard audio systems and run multimedia content on a computer equipped with a CD-ROM drive.
With encoded music, N2K is going beyond many other companies in the record industry, which have limited their use of the Internet to promotional purposes.
Many record companies are fearful of piracy on the Internet, which will eventually make downloading and copying digitally recorded works easier.
Encoded Music's first titles will be released in early 1997. Each title will link music fans to individual artists' Web sites, created and maintained by N2K's interactive design and technology team.
These sites will be regularly updated to include current news and information about the particular artist.

As an engineer and producer, Ramone pioneered the use of solid-state mixing consoles, was the first to employ Dolby four-track sound for a film in 1976 with Barbara Streisand's "A Star Is Born" and became the first producer in history to use fiber optics to record tracks in real time from different locations with Frank Sinatra's two "Duets" albums.

"Success in the music business has always rested on a strong relationship between the artist, the music, and the audience," said Ramone. "With the added power of the Internet, this relationship can be completed by tying in the global Web audience."
